items.body: A nontrivial lower bound can be found in a paper of Cam Stewart (see http://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/PM_Dept/Homepages/Stewart/Jour_Books/J-reine-ange-Math-1980.pdf). He proves, more generally, for fixed bases a and b for which $\log a/\log b$ is irrational, that the sum of the number of nonzero digits in the base a and base b digits of an integer n exceeds (essentially) $$\log \log n/ \log \log \log n.$$
